title: Harris County Sues Trump Administration Over Anti-Terrorism Funds
description_short: Harris County Sues Trump Administration Over Anti-Terrorism Funds
description_medium: Harris County is suing the Trump administration over its threat to withhold anti-terrorism funds. The administration has demanded that the county overhaul its election procedures in order to receive the funds. The county has argued that this is an abuse of power and an attempt to interfere with its election processes.

title: Says 'Russia, if you're listening'
description_short: At a press conference, Trump publicly urged Russia to find Clinton email files.
description_medium: At a July 27, 2016, press conference in Doral, Florida, Donald Trump urged Russia to find approximately 30,000 emails Hillary Clinton had said were missing. He added that Russia would “probably be rewarded mightily by our press.” The remark publicly invited a foreign government to seek material related to his presidential-election opponent.
description_long: During a July 27, 2016, press conference in Doral, Florida, Donald Trump discussed Hillary Clinton’s use of a private email server and the deletion of messages after a subpoena. He said that if Russia or another country had the emails, he would like to see them, then addressed Russia directly: “If Russia is listening, I hope you’re able to find the 30,000 emails that are missing.” He added that Russia would “probably be rewarded mightily by our press.” The remarks were made during the presidential campaign and publicly encouraged a foreign government to seek emails connected to Trump’s Democratic opponent. Trump framed the request in the context of allegations about Clinton’s email handling and reports of hacking into a political party. The statement itself is documented in the press-conference transcript. It does not, by itself, establish a private agreement, operational coordination with Russia, or that any later Russian action was caused by the request.

title: Signs Asylum Cooperative Agreement with El Salvador
description_short: The U.S. signed an Asylum Cooperative Agreement with El Salvador, redirecting asylum seekers to apply there.
description_medium: On September 20, 2019, the United States signed an Asylum Cooperative Agreement with El Salvador. The Trump administration described the arrangement as redirecting at least some asylum seekers to seek protection there rather than applying through the U.S. system. The supplied account does not state who qualified or how the transfers worked.
